A.explanation: Acceleration per unit mass is $a/m$, which has units far from the newton and is smaller for larger mass, opposite to $F = ma$.

B.explanation: Change in kinetic energy per unit time is power $P = \Delta E/\Delta t$, measured in watts, not force.

C.explanation: Newton's second law states resultant force equals rate of change of momentum, $F = \Delta p/\Delta t$.

D.explanation: Change in velocity per unit time is acceleration $a = \Delta v/\Delta t$, which must be multiplied by mass $m$ to give force.

hints: Notice each option says per unit time or per unit mass, so translate it as divided by time $\Delta t$ or divided by mass $m$.
Recall Newton's second law in momentum form: resultant force is linked to momentum $p = mv$, not to energy or to velocity alone.
Compare $\Delta p/\Delta t$ with $m \times \Delta v/\Delta t$ for constant mass to see which option gives $ma$ with unit $\text{N}$.
walkthrough: The question asks which rate equals the resultant force that causes acceleration.
State Newton's second law in its general form: $F = \Delta p/\Delta t$, where momentum is $p = mv$.
For constant mass, $\Delta p/\Delta t = m\Delta v/\Delta t = ma$, which has unit $\text{kg m s}^{-2} = \text{N}$, as required for force.
Check the other wordings: change in velocity per unit time is only $a$, acceleration per unit mass is $a/m$, and change in kinetic energy per unit time is power.
Only the change in momentum per unit time matches $F$ in definition, units and physical meaning. This is option C.
